lstsq over all device x block partials: line-end port reads hand-off slot of compute idx 1 before pack (stale = previous call own block). Cumulative ready counter: fast cores next-block signals substitute for a slow core current-block signal
compute core signals next block of a kind only after the kind consumers acked all earlier blocks of the kind

result: dev 53 pass, non-dev 53 pass x2, debug 3 pass

what: Hand-off contract is racy: (a) one cumulative sem_block_ack shared by fwd/bwd/final consumers lets one kind acks release another kind slot; (b) cumulative ready counting from many producers lets a fast core next-block signal substitute for a slow core current-block signal. Both produced wrong results on device (b only without watcher).
suggest: Planner guidance for many-producer/few-consumer cumulative semaphores: one ack counter per independent consumer stream, and gate producer N+1 signal on consumer ack of N (or per-slot counters).

what: CKL_ELTWISE_CHAIN_SKIP_COMPUTE doc says CB counts unchanged and the dataflow handshake stays intact, but in a streaming binary chain it hung the multi-chip pipeline (pack thread no longer synchronized with unpack inputs), making it unusable as an ablation tool here.
suggest: Document that skip mode can desynchronize pack vs unpack lifecycles, or keep a math/pack sync in skip mode.
